# Documentation Drift

Docs describe the **intended** system; code implements a subset; the docs are never walked back.
Found in 12 of 15 repositories, with 11 distinct instances in two of them. This is the
characteristic failure mode of the source set, and the direct cost of
[[import-finished-work-into-git]] — nothing forces a doc to be re-read when the work lands in one
commit.

## The sharpest instances

**A test suite that does not exist.** `Farley/README.md` line 174: "Tested with **Vitest** and
**Playwright**." There is no vitest, no playwright, and zero test files; `CONTRIBUTING.md` says the
opposite outright. Resolved at interview:

> "Aspirational — tests were planned."
> — interview, 2026-07-28

**A shipped feature that is a stub.** `Farley`'s README and four docs describe Android ML Kit OCR as
the on-device engine. ML Kit is in no `build.gradle` and `OcrReader.readNow()` returns `null`. The
working reader is the accessibility node-tree parser — see [[node-tree-read-before-ocr]].

**A deleted transport still in the build.** `browser_game_stickfps/server/Dockerfile` keeps
`EXPOSE 10000/udp` after UDP was removed, and all four `.tooling` agent files still instruct agents
to use "Geckos.io" and "Fly.io" — see [[websocket-tcp-over-geckos-udp]].

**Undocumented cache generations.** `Physics/exam_prep/sw.js` declares `physprep-v4`; `snapshot.md`
says `v3`; the README says `v2`. At least two offline-cache changes were never recorded.
`TODO:` what broke between them is unresolved — "Don't remember the cache history" (interview,
2026-07-28), so no narrative is asserted here.

**A documented file that was never committed.** `Information-Systems-Modelling/lab6/README.md` lists
`snapshot.md` in its file tree. It does not exist, on disk or in history.

**A guide predating its own code.** `IT Applications in Business and Commerce/.../guide.txt` is
stamped "Updated 2026-05-13", describes the *pre-rewrite* baseline as "What exists today", is
banner-stamped for one track while its body targets another, depends on a `recon_lap.py` that does
not exist, and hardcodes a machine-local `D:\...` path.

**Counts that disagree with themselves.** `Physics` alone: `sims.js` documented as 9 simulators in
one section and 13 in another; `qa.mjs` as 32 checks vs 34; the bank as 62 questions vs a generated
audit reporting 75.

**A licence claim three months stale.** `Optimization Methods/first_project/README.md` still says
"No license file is currently included in this repository" long after MIT was added at the root.

**The rejected design shipped in a sibling format.** `Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence`
argues at length against modelling RSI as a dimension, then ships `Dim RSI.dim` doing exactly that —
which is also an instance of [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]] and is covered on
[[rsi-as-measure-not-dimension]].

## The counter-habit that bounds it

`browser_game_stickfps` never rewrites a retired decision — it stacks a dated **SUPERSEDED banner**
on top of the original text. `docs/SRS.md` FR-9.3, `DESIGN_PROMPT.md` §3 and `docs/DESIGN-BRIEF.md`
§2 all still carry the grayscale mandate under such a banner. This trades internal consistency for an
auditable history; see [[superseded-in-place-documentation]].

## Where drift is absent

`Oracle-Database-Laboratories` — docs match code closely, essentially no drift. It is also the repo
whose prose is written *as inline SQL comments* rather than as a separate document, which removes the
gap where drift lives.
